bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Ramp Gigafactory for captive auto use; Priority 2: Scale Shakti/Mahashakti; Priority 3: Raise separate capital for Cell subsidiary expansion beyond 6GWh.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Supply chain ramp speed to clear backlog; Commodity price volatility (Lithium upcycle); Execution risk on 6GWh yield stabilization; Regulatory shifts in PLI/ACC schemes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, turnaround-focused, emphasizing 'structural advantages' and 'operating leverage'; transparent on past service issues now resolved.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 90%+ of OpEx is fixed, creating massive operating leverage as volumes rebound; Accounting change on warranty revenue recognition created a one-time ₹20-30cr drag but improves future visibility; EV Bike segment tripling in size with Ola holding 50%+ share.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "During the quarter, we successfully completed a Rs 780 crore Qualified Institutional Placement", with strong institutional demand resulting in 56% oversubscription; the deck says the capital "strengthens our balance sheet and provides additional financial flexibility to support disciplined growth".
- Stated philosophy: "Our focus is not growth at any cost, but durable growth-built on discipline, technology and an EV market whose structural foundations continue to strengthen."
- Forward priorities framed as "continue becoming leaner, scale volumes without rebuilding the earlier cost structure, deepen vertical integration and translate these advantages into margin expansion and lower cash burn".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Auto: Near FCF positive, 1Mn unit capacity ready, Gen 3 warranty costs down to ₹59cr (from ₹500cr+); Cell: 2.5GWh operational, 6GWh commissioning by June, 15% of vehicles now use Bharat Cells, targeting 10-15% cost advantage at scale.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising lithium prices and import dependency | Ola Electric Mobility Ltd | beneficiary | High | Vertical integration with own Gigafactory provides 10-15% cost advantage and insulation from global cell shortages. |
| Service network inefficiencies hurting brand | Ola Electric Mobility Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Service backlogs down 88%, same-day closure at 87%, driving V-shaped volume recovery. |
| High CapEx intensity in EV manufacturing | Competitors lacking cell integration | loser | High | Competitors face new CapEx cycles for cells while Ola's asset base supports ₹15k-20k cr revenue without incremental spend. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck frames FY26 as "a year of reset" and Q1 FY27 as "the first full quarter after that reset", with Ola registrations up 97% QoQ against a broader E2W market that grew 17%, taking market share from 5.1% in Q4 FY26 to 8.4% in Q1 FY27.
- Closing remarks position the company as "a vertically integrated technology and energy company", with the Cell business extending relevance "beyond mobility" into utility-scale storage, defence drones and near-space platforms.
- Category tailwind cited: "India's E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time in June"; Odisha given as a proof point where state penetration "surged from 10% in Feb 2026 to 20%+ in June 2026".
- Growth described as broad-based rather than single-geography: West grew ~61% QoQ, North and South ~54% each and East ~34%, with the North and East called "our strongest share pools" and South/West the scale-up opportunity.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy] Deck cites a strengthening central and state policy backdrop: "Delhi's pathway towards fully electric new two-wheeler registrations, Maharashtra's EV policy and Haryana's 100% motor-vehicle-tax concession for eligible EVs".
- [PLI] "We received a one-time benefit to our cost base from PLI-related levies, supported by a favourable government stance towards our Cell business", which the deck links to localisation and an indigenous battery ecosystem.
- [Macro] "The conflict in West Asia contributed to volatility in fuel availability and prices, sharpening the cost-of-ownership advantage of EVs."
- [Market size] "India is expected to require more than 400 GWh of energy storage by 2032", framed as the long-term opportunity for domestically manufactured storage.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin 38.5% (structural via vertical integration); OpEx reset from ₹844cr (Q4FY25) to ₹428cr (Q4FY26), targeting ₹300-350cr run-rate; Warranty costs reduced 88% YoY.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Q1FY27 rev ₹500-550cr (nearly double Q4); Margin: Hold industry-leading GM >35%; Order Inflow: 40k-45k orders expected in Q1FY27; Capex: Auto maintenance ~₹50cr/yr, Cell Capex for 6GWh completing in Q1/Q2 FY27, no further major CapEx until subsidiary fundraising.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Production backlog exists due to supply chain ramp; Inventory days reduced to 3-4 days; April registrations up 20% MoM despite industry decline; May trending 14k-15k registrations.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Roadster (EV Bike) contributing 15% of orders with 50%+ segment share; Shakti (B2B storage) ramping post-auto allocation; Mahashakti (Grid) in development; External cell sales pipeline emerging.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Ola Electric achieved its first operating cash flow positive quarter (₹91cr CFO) driven by a structural gross margin expansion to 38.5% and a 50% YoY OpEx reset, validating the Gen 3 platform economics. With breakeven lowered to 20k-25k units/month and a visible order backlog, the company is pivoting from survival to scaling its integrated auto-cell-energy stack without significant incremental CapEx.

rows.text: launches a **battery energy storage portfolio**, Ola Shakti for homes, Shakti Rack for commercial and industrial use and Mahashakti for utility scale, built on its own cell and pack capability, with no pricing disclosed.
